solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Resist change in partnership? Precisely

parts.note: in cricket a stand is a partnership between two batsmen at the crease
to have something off pat is to know it precisely, so pat means exactly

explanation.surface: A question about whether a business partner would resist change, answered with a curt 'Precisely'.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket, a British bat-and-ball game, calls the runs two batsmen add together a stand, so 'partnership' is not about business here.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom, originally from poker, meaning to stick with what you have and refuse to alter course.

clue.text: Small enough specimen

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
ample means more than enough, plenty

explanation.surface: A specimen that is just about big enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a small portion taken to show what the whole is like.

clue.text: Every other substitute

definitions.meaning: every second one, as in on alternating days
a stand-in or replacement, someone who takes another's place

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means every second one; as a noun, mainly American, it means a stand-in.

clue.text: Two infer one duke should leave

indicators.note: should leave means one piece goes out of the other

parts.note: to deduce is to infer or conclude

explanation.surface: Two people infer that a single duke ought to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A two in a deck of cards or on dice is called by this name.

clue.text: What journalist writes may make it clear

indicators.note: may make suggests the given letters can be built into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A journalist's writing that might explain things clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece in a newspaper or magazine is what a reporter produces.

clue.text: Legendary character, singer, shunning love on island

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it, so the island letter leads
shunning means avoiding, so the letter for love is dropped from the singer's name

parts.note: Enrico Caruso was the famous Italian operatic tenor
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A legendary singer on an island who keeps away from romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Shunning O takes CARUSO down to CARUS, and I for island comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Icarus is the figure from Greek myth who flew too near the sun on wax wings.

clue.text: Woodworker has to find fault with log

parts.note: to carp is to complain or find fault
to log something is to enter it in a record

explanation.surface: A woodworker forced to complain about a piece of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'log' looks like timber for the woodworker, but it is the verb meaning record.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesperson who makes and repairs wooden structures.

clue.text: Cycled round in riding competition

parts.note: rode, the past tense of ride, as in rode a bike
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A cyclist doing laps during an equestrian contest.
explanation.definitionFit: An event where cowboys show skill at riding broncos and roping cattle.

clue.text: The smallest possible number in a set of bones?

definitions.meaning: the bony framework of a body

explanation.surface: A question about the minimum number of bones that make a set.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton staff is the bare minimum, and the frame of bones in a body bears the same name.

clue.text: Appropriate word recently found in foreign tome

indicators.note: found in tells us one piece sits inside the other piece
foreign suggests something strange or altered, so the letters of tome are rearranged

parts.note: just, as in 'just arrived', means recently

explanation.surface: A well-chosen word that has lately turned up in a book from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges the book's name into MOTE, and 'found in' sets the word for recently inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for the exactly right expression in a given context.

clue.text: Bishop and rook not employed in check

parts.note: B is the chess notation for a bishop
R is the chess notation for a rook
someone idle is out of work, not employed

explanation.surface: A chess scene: bishop and rook sit unused while a king is in check.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to restrain or hold back, as one curbs a horse with its headgear.

clue.text: Second answer to be given is a staple food

parts.note: to go can mean to be given, as when a prize goes to the winner

explanation.surface: A second answer still to come is about a basic food.
explanation.definitionFit: A starch from palm pith, a basic food in parts of the tropics.

clue.text: Generous lager poured out

indicators.note: beer poured out is spilled about, suggesting the letters of lager scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone pouring a generous glass of lager.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a generous helping is a big one.

clue.text: Shepherd in timeless novel's beginning?

indicators.note: timeless is read as without time, and T is the abbreviation for time, so that letter goes

parts.note: a novel begins with its first numbered chapter

explanation.surface: A shepherd appearing at the start of a classic novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening of a novel is CHAPTER ONE; remove T (time) and it becomes CHAPERONE.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to escort and look after someone, just as a shepherd guides a flock.

clue.text: US film star embracing maiden in punt

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: Clark Gable was the American star of Gone with the Wind
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star hugging a young woman on a flat-bottomed boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, written M. 'punt' looks like the river boat, but here it is the British slang for a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a punt is a bet or a speculative try at something.

clue.text: Unlucky on Elizabeth's famous mare

parts.note: black, as in a black day, means ill-fated
Bess is a pet form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: An unlucky bet on Queen Elizabeth's famous horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The mare belonged to Dick Turpin, an 18th-century English highwayman, said to have ridden her from London to York.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary horse ridden by the highwayman Dick Turpin.

clue.text: Gone hot in resort, being very active

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, sorting the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who finds it so hot at a holiday resort that they have gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place, but read as re-sort it rearranges GONE HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for busy and constantly moving about, never still.

clue.text: Form quite unpredictable — better ignoring both sides

indicators.note: unpredictable letters go anywhere, so the word quite is rearranged
ignoring both sides means the first and last letters of the word are dropped

explanation.surface: Behaviour that is quite unpredictable, and better if it disregards both parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unpredictable' rearranges QUITE to ETIQU; 'ignoring both sides' takes BETTER down to ETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Good form means correct manners, and the code of polite behaviour has this name.

clue.text: Liking priest's initial charm

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of priest

parts.note: to enchant is to charm or delight

explanation.surface: A fondness for a priest's first charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A fondness or strong inclination for something.

clue.text: Stone, green and red, male unexpectedly produced

indicators.note: something produced unexpectedly comes out in a surprising form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A green and red stone that a man has surprisingly brought out.
explanation.definitionFit: The precious gem is a green beryl, and its name is also used for its bright colour.

clue.text: Author had upped and left

indicators.note: upped in a down clue means the word had is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A writer who rose and walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl was the British author of Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.

clue.text: Writer's block? No end

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the writer to the wordplay

indicators.note: no end means the final letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a barrier blocks the way

explanation.surface: A question about writer's block that apparently never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's block' reads as one phrase, but 'Writer' is the definition and 'block' gives BARRIER. J. M. Barrie wrote Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie was the Scottish novelist and playwright, the creator of Peter Pan.

clue.text: Bird from extremely cold north

parts.note: bitter weather is extremely cold

explanation.surface: A bird that has come from the frozen north.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading bird of the heron family, known for its booming call.

clue.text: Where 27 was killed in Dover, on arrival

indicators.note: in says the letters are held within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A murder victim slain in Dover just as he arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 across is Mercutio, killed in the city where Romeo and Juliet is set.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city is the setting of Romeo and Juliet, where Mercutio dies.

clue.text: Marksman needs two attempts

parts.note: a crack, as in 'have a crack at it', is an attempt
a shot, as in 'give it a shot', is an attempt

explanation.surface: A marksman who needs a second go to hit the target.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for an expert sharpshooter, someone highly accurate with a gun.

clue.text: Player's agent overlooking fine

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the player to the wordplay

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving out, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: a factor is an agent who buys and sells for another
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A sports player's agent who lets a penalty pass.
explanation.walkthrough: A factor is a business agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A player in a stage production is a performer of a role.

clue.text: Give rise to lawsuit involving university

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a case is an action in a court of law

explanation.surface: A legal action against a university that stirs up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to bring something about or make it happen.

clue.text: See two Commanding Officers over a drink

indicators.note: in a down clue the officers sit over the letter, so they come first

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for Commanding Officer
a second CO, for the other Commanding Officer

explanation.surface: Two senior officers being invited over for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot beverage made from powdered cacao beans.

clue.text: Song from worker on border

parts.note: a worker ant is the usual crossword worker
a hem is the folded border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A tune coming from a labourer stationed at a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A national or rousing hymn sung in praise or loyalty.

clue.text: Shakespeare character wounded — in Rome, I suspect

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to be cut is to be wounded

explanation.surface: A murder-mystery hunch: a Shakespeare character has been wounded in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' shuffles the city and the I into MERIO; 'in' puts the word for wounded within. He is Romeo's friend, fittingly stabbed in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo's witty friend in Romeo and Juliet, fatally stabbed by Tybalt.

clue.text: Push one's way through American street

parts.note: thru is the American informal spelling of through

explanation.surface: Someone forcing a path down an American street.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to shove or force forward through an obstacle or crowd.

clue.text: American involved kept secret

indicators.note: involved suggests something intricate and tangled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An American who took part in something that was covered up.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin legal phrase for proceedings held privately, away from the public.
